thread:
Maya Chen: Hey folks — quick ping for review on PR #2385: changes to routing policy, adaptive cache TTL, and adds a 4-bit quant profile for the GGML runner. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2385

Short summary & ask: can someone check perf regressions and the KV-eviction logic? Also need an approval to merge before tomorrow's staging deploy window (10:00 PDT).

Perf microbench (local, seq_len=512, batch=8):
```
before: p50=45ms p95=120ms tokens/s=420
after:  p50=38ms p95=135ms tokens/s=468
notes: tail p95 increased ~12ms, overall throughput improved 11%
```

What changed:
- routing: route small requests to small-model pool earlier (threshold 128 tokens)
- cache: adaptive TTL based on seq prefix hit-rate (config flag: adaptive_cache=true)
- quant: new 4-bit profile tuned for latency (quant_profile=v4a)

CI: tests passed locally for me; one flaky on CI (see below). I'll paste the PR description section for quick reading.

Samir Patel: I'll take an initial pass today. Quick q: does adaptive TTL risk evicting prefixes while they're still warming? :thinking: 

Jess Rivera: @Maya Chen can you add a short note in the PR about fallback behavior when small-model pool saturated? We should be explicit about cost vs latency tradeoff.

Liam O'Neill: CI is failing on allocator_test in linux-x86-64, leg: runtime-wheels. Log:
```
ASSERT: free_list.empty() at allocator.cc:214
```
Not sure if it's flaky or related to the cache change.

CI Bot: runtime-wheels: failed — see https://ci.redwood.io/build/3321. Re-run with comment "rerun-ci".

Ana García: @Maya Chen can you post the benchmark command you used? I'd like to re-run on the dedicated cluster (g4dn-like setup).

Maya Chen: Benchmark command I used:
```
./bench_runner --model /models/ggml-v3.q4_0 --seq 512 --batch 8 --routes small_pool
```
Results run on dev-box (A100-sim); will queue on dedicated. Also ran canary with cache disabled; tail latency was lower but throughput dropped 9%.

Samir Patel: I'll look at the eviction heuristics and leave inline comments. If p95 increases only on some prefixes we should tighten TTL floor.

Jess Rivera: If CI is flaky please add an ignore marker for allocator_test while we triage? Prefer not, but might unblock staging.

Liam O'Neill: Rerun CI now.

CI Bot: runtime-wheels: passed on rerun — https://ci.redwood.io/build/3321

Samir Patel: Left comments on PR re: TTL floor and explicit unit test for eviction racecases.

Maya Chen: Thanks. @Samir Patel @Liam O'Neill can we aim to merge after QA validates canary tonight? I'm ok to merge tomorrow morning if QA green.

Ana García: I'll run dedicated-cluster bench and post numbers in this thread by 19:30 PDT.

Jess Rivera: :eyes: will follow QA results.

Maya Chen: tagging for visibility: @eng-runtime @eng-sre — any objections to merging tomorrow if canary passes?

Samir Patel: no objections from me. :thumbsup:

Liam O'Neill: no objections. :shipit:

Maya Chen: Great — I'll wait for Ana and then schedule merge. Thanks everyone!
